Assertions authored, all mutation-resistant (exact values, no truthiness):
1. Closed vocabulary: FOUNDATION_OUTCOME_KINDS === exactly [EXPECTED_RED, HONEST_UNKNOWN, PASS_EXPECTED, PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT].
2. Distinct artifact: version === "moe-foundation-expected-outcome/1"; the canonicalized manifest contains neither "moe-schedule-coverage/1" nor any "SCHEDULE_" substring, so no code or coverage authority is borrowed from the schedule-checker's source-derived universe.
3. One outcome per entry: entry ids unique, sorted, and equal to fixtureIds ∪ scheduleIds.
4. Partition completeness: union of the three journey partitions equals the manifest entry-id list exactly, plus per-journey size pins (FOUNDATION_PARTITION_COUNTS) so a dropped schedule cannot slip through silently.
5. Labels + pinned sha256 through the LANDED helpers only (identifyFoundationFixture wraps identifyCanonicalEvidence), and a volatility test: re-labelling a fixture with recordedAt/seed leaves the digest unchanged (schedule-model identity precedent).
6. Probe integrity in three directions — every ABSENT entry resolves to a declared probe AND every declared probe is claimed by an entry (no orphans either way); each probe reports absent on an unrelated export set; each probe goes RED when its named export appears; and pattern-bearing probes go RED on a differently-named export that still matches, which is the guard against ratchet rot when the eventual production name differs from my guess.
7. Determinism (two builds byte-identical via canonicalize + digest equality), zero BENCH-* identifiers in any foundation source or in the manifest, and held-out enforcement by source scan: no non-test .ts under packages/** may import anything matching foundation/.
8. Zero-work false-green oracle, both directions: an empty-diff/no-artifact/no-receipt/green-claiming trace must yield refusal J1_ZERO_WORK_FALSE_GREEN; a real-work trace with exactly three human actions must be accepted.

Design decision recorded for step 3-4 (keeps import discipline intact): the probe is a declarative spec (package name + absent export names + optional pattern) plus a pure evaluator over a caller-supplied export-name list. testkit never imports @moe/core or @moe/scheduler; the fault tests feed Object.keys of the real package namespaces into the same evaluator. Probe targets are bare package names, never deep internal paths, so the scheduler package-boundary rule is honoured rather than side-stepped via the exempt tests/ root.

foundation-model-j1.ts — J1 per design 18.2. Exactly three human actions (goal.create, graph.approve, acceptance.final). evaluateJ1Journey refusal ORDER is part of the spec: zero-work first, so a no-op trace is named J1_ZERO_WORK_FALSE_GREEN rather than being absorbed by a downstream missing-proof complaint. isZeroWorkAttempt = no changed path AND no artifact AND no receipt. hasGatingReceipt accepts only OBSERVED / DAEMON_VERIFIED / HUMAN_APPROVED, so an AGENT_REPORTED-only trace refuses with J1_AGENT_TEXT_AS_GATE (CORE-I14); a null acceptance proof refuses with J1_ACCEPTANCE_WITHOUT_PROOF (CORE-I4).

foundation-model-j3j4.ts — J3 per design 18.2/18.3: four declared crash boundaries (TRANSACTION_BEGIN/WRITE/COMMIT, EFFECT_ACK) chosen because they are the subset the landed durable-store surface can actually be killed at; the wider catalogue is left out rather than claimed. classifyRestartRecord pivots on whole-or-none durability: an unknown external effect never adopts (RECONCILIATION when the commit is durable, QUARANTINED when it is not), an unobserved commit never adopts, and unacknowledged / UNKNOWN-truth records are SUSPECT. evaluateJ3Continuation enforces "one safe action creating a traceable binding, never edited history". J4 per design 18.2: findings must link evidence, delta approval must carry changed hashes, invalidated and carry-forward sets must be disjoint, history must stay readable, and round > 3 requires explicit escalation.
